issues.on_page: Cemetery: Salaries and benefits 2,073; Insurance 616 (detail[86], detail[87])
issues.issue: The extractor rules put cemetery under health/welfare. The extractor used culture/recreation so the lines tie to the statement's 'Environment and leisure' function (421,058, p5), which does include Cemetery. Defensible, but it departs from the rule and has no review flag.

issues.on_page: Landfill: Salaries and benefits 3,479; Insurance 516; Supplies 8
issues.issue: Landfill would normally be utilities (refuse) or health/welfare. Mapping it to streets/highways ties to the statement's Public works General Fund 4,003 (p5). detail[88] is flagged for review; detail[89] and detail[90] are not.

Every 'Salaries and benefits' line (one per department, detail[22], [31], [37], [53], [61], [70], [79], [86], [88]) mixes salaries with employee benefits but is recorded only as salaries and wages, with no review flag.
'Transportation' for police, fire and rescue is probably vehicle and fuel costs, not training and travel. It could be fuel or repairs and maintenance (detail[33], [42], [50]).

issues.on_page: Budgetary Comparison Schedule - All Funds, governmental lines (Total governmental actual 1,422,634; resources incl. Bond anticipation note proceeds 2,500,000)
issues.issue: The Street Fund and Debt Service Fund have no detail schedule. The all-funds budget schedule is the only budget-vs-actual source, but its governmental lines combine all funds and cannot be split by fund, so they were left out (explained in notes). Defensible, but there is no budget detail for those two funds. The 2,500,000 bond anticipation note proceeds (business-type) appear only on the budget and cash flow schedules, as the notes say.
